title: A tiny moon of Saturn tugs a fresh streamer out of a ring on every orbit

cover.alt: Black-and-white Cassini image: a bright horizontal band of Saturn’s F ring across the top, and a small bright moon below it.

body: Prometheus is an oblong moon only about 102 km across, orbiting Saturn just inside the narrow F ring once every 14.7 hours. Its orbit is slightly oval, and once each lap it reaches its farthest point from Saturn, closest to the ring, where its gravity is **just strong enough to pull a streamer of dust out of the ring**. The ring material orbits more slowly than the moon, so the streamer falls behind and stretches, leaving a dark channel beside it. Next time round, Prometheus pulls a new streamer about 3.2 degrees farther along, so the ring ends up lined with a whole series of them, sometimes 10 to 15 at once.

slides.alt: Black-and-white time-lapse: a small moon drifts up from below towards a bright horizontal ring, the picture goes black for a few seconds, and when it returns a curved streamer of material hangs from the ring down towards the moon, which has moved away below.
slides.caption: Cassini time-lapse, Nov 2006: Prometheus closes in on the F ring and draws out a streamer. The screen goes black as both pass through Saturn’s shadow. About 12.5 hours of images, slowed 1.5×.
slides.credit: NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute · Public domain · excerpt, slowed 1.5×

slides.prompt: The streamer first points ahead of Prometheus, then falls farther and farther behind it. Why?
slides.answer: The ring orbits more slowly than the moon
slides.detail: Prometheus is a little closer to Saturn than the ring’s core, and closer orbits are faster, so the moon keeps pulling ahead of the dust it disturbed.

slides.heading: One lap of the ring sculptor

slides.label: Cassini images in the movie, one every 10.5 minutes
slides.text: Together they cover about 12.5 hours on 23 and 24 November 2006, just under half of one streamer-and-channel cycle.

slides.question: What eventually wipes out each streamer and channel?
options: Shearing as the ring material orbits
slides.explanation: Particles at slightly different distances from Saturn orbit at slightly different speeds. That shear spreads the dust out until the streamer fades away.
